### 1 — Scene
A breakfast meal: two fried eggs, two slices of raisin toast, two toasted English-muffin halves, orange juice, and individual portions of butter and apricot jam.

### 2 — Vessel
The main plate appears approximately **23 cm** in diameter.  
Plate area = 3.14 × 11.5² ≈ **415 cm²**. The drink and condiment portions are counted separately.

### 3–6 — Items, area, volume, and weight
Area shares below represent the plate footprint, with stacked bread included in the height.

| Item | Plate area | Area × typical height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Two fried eggs | 25% | 104 cm² × 1.0 cm = 104 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 104 g |
| Two raisin-toast slices | 32% | 133 cm² × 2.2 cm = 293 ml | 0.30 g/ml | 88 g |
| English-muffin halves | 20% | 83 cm² × 2.0 cm = 166 ml | 0.40 g/ml | 66 g |

The food footprints total **77% of the plate**, consistent with the visible coverage.

Separately:
- **Orange juice:** approximately 250 ml × 1.04 g/ml = **260 g**.
- **Two butter portions:** approximately **20 g** combined, excluding packaging.
- **Two apricot-jam portions:** approximately **40 g** combined, excluding packaging.

No separate pool of cooking oil is visible; the fried-egg energy estimate includes modest cooking fat.

### 7 — Energy
| Item | kcal/100 g | Estimated kcal |

### 8 — Sanity check
Estimated total: **578 g and 964 kcal**, including juice and all visible condiment contents. This is plausible for a bread-heavy breakfast with butter and jam. The bread identification and condiment sizes are the main uncertainties.
